from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping", 
                          ["A sphere has pairs of opposite, antipodal points.", 
                           "Imagine points on the North and South Poles.", 
                           "Antipodal points are exactly on the opposite side."])
        
        # Sphere setup
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'A2', 'D5')
        self.add(sphere)
        
        # Antipodal points
        p1 = Dot(point=sphere.get_top(), color=RED)
        p2 = Dot(point=sphere.get_bottom(), color=RED)
        self.add(p1, p2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(Create(p1), Create(p2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Rotate sphere to show points moving
        sphere.save_state()
        self.play(Rotate(sphere, angle=PI/2, axis=RIGHT), 
                  Rotate(p1, angle=PI/2, axis=RIGHT, about_point=sphere.get_center()),
                  Rotate(p2, angle=PI/2, axis=RIGHT, about_point=sphere.get_center()))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlighting the relationship
        line = Line(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Borsuk-Ulam Theorem", [
            "Borsuk-Ulam maps n-spheres to n-dimensional space.",
            "It guarantees a mapping of at least one antipodal pair.",
            "Temperature and pressure match at two opposite points."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        point1 = Dot(color="#FF5733")
        point2 = Dot(color="#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        # Place points antipodally on the sphere
        pos1 = sphere.get_center() + np.array([1.5, 0, 0])
        pos2 = sphere.get_center() - np.array([1.5, 0, 0])
        point1.move_to(pos1)
        point2.move_to(pos2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point1), FadeIn(point2))
        
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFC300").move_to(pos1)
        self.play(Create(pulse), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(pulse))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFC300")
        line = Line(pos1, pos2, color="#33FF57")
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(sphere), FadeOut(point1), FadeOut(point2), FadeOut(line))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Thieves divide a necklace with different beads.",
            "They want an equal share of every bead type.",
            "We can cut the necklace at most k times."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Stolen Necklace Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a necklace represented by a line of colored beads
        beads = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=1) for color in [GOLD, BLUE]*5])
        beads.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(beads, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(beads))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show two thieves dividing segments to equalize the value
        alice = Text("Alice", color=BLUE, font_size=20)
        bob = Text("Bob", color=GOLD, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(alice, 'A3')
        self.place_at_grid(bob, 'E3')
        
        # Split beads
        split_beads = VGroup(beads[:5].copy(), beads[5:].copy())
        self.play(
            FadeOut(beads),
            FadeIn(alice),
            FadeIn(bob),
            split_beads[0].animate.move_to(self.grid['B3']),
            split_beads[1].animate.move_to(self.grid['D3'])
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate cutting the necklace
        cut = Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=RED)
        cut.move_to(self.grid['C3'])
        self.play(Create(cut))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Bridging Theory and Problem", [
            "Model the necklace as an interval on a sphere.",
            "Borsuk-Ulam proves a fair division must exist.",
            "The exact cut points are hard to find."
        ])
        
        # Elements for animation
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        necklace = Line(start=LEFT*1.5, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=8)
        beads = VGroup(*[Dot(point=LEFT*1.5 + i*0.25*RIGHT, color=YELLOW) for i in range(12)])
        necklace_group = VGroup(necklace, beads)
        
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(necklace_group, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), FadeIn(necklace_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFC300"))
        # Move beads along the sphere surface
        self.play(
            Rotate(necklace_group, angle=PI/2, about_point=self.grid['C3']),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        # Show antipodal points
        dot1 = Dot(color=RED).move_to(circle.get_top())
        dot2 = Dot(color=RED).move_to(circle.get_bottom())
        self.play(FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2))
        self.play(Indicate(dot1), Indicate(dot2))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Borsuk-Ulam is a powerful existence theorem in topology.",
            "It guarantees that fair divisions are always possible.",
            "Topology proves the existence of impossible solutions."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Summary", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # Create objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE)
        necklace = VMobject().set_points_as_corners([UP*1, LEFT*1.5, DOWN*1, RIGHT*1.5, UP*1]).set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        sphere_obj = self.place_in_area(sphere, 'A2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(sphere_obj))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        necklace_obj = self.place_in_area(necklace, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(necklace_obj))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.play(FadeOut(sphere_obj), FadeOut(necklace_obj))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a sphere (S²) and the 'antipodal point'—the point exactly on the opposite side of a sphere. Visualize this as placing a glowing point on the North Pole and its twin on the South Pole.
sections.example: Imagine a world map wrapped on a sphere. If you stand at the North Pole, your antipode is the South Pole.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
sections.content: Explain the theorem: Any continuous mapping from an n-sphere to n-dimensional Euclidean space must map at least one pair of antipodal points to the same location. Focus on the 2D case (S² to R²).
sections.example: Visual animation: A globe with varying temperature/pressure data. The theorem guarantees there are at least two opposite points on Earth right now with the exact same temperature and air pressure.

sections.title: The Stolen Necklace Problem
sections.content: Transition to the application: Two thieves steal a necklace with different types of beads. They must divide the loot so that each gets an equal share of every type of bead. The necklace can be cut at most k times (where k is the number of bead types).
sections.example: A visual chain of 10 gold beads and 10 silver beads. An animation shows the necklace being 'unfolded' into a line, and the cuts being made to distribute beads equally between two characters, 'Alice' and 'Bob'.

sections.title: Bridging Theory and Problem
sections.content: Explain how the necklace is modeled as an interval, then mapped to a sphere, allowing the Borsuk-Ulam theorem to prove that a fair division exists mathematically, even if finding the cuts is computationally difficult.
sections.example: Use a 'color-coded bar' animation where segments shift until the Borsuk-Ulam condition is satisfied, showing the 'Fair Division' point being reached.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
sections.content: Summarize that Borsuk-Ulam is a powerful existence theorem in topology. It doesn't tell us where to cut, but it guarantees that a perfectly fair 'theft' is always possible.
sections.example: Final slide: 'Topology: Proving the impossible exists, even when we can't find it easily.'
